'''Jiro Tsuji''' (May 11, 1927 – April 1, 2022)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=August 8, 2022 |title=Obituary: Jiro Tsuji |url=https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/Obituary-Jiro-Tsuji/100/i27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609182017/https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/Obituary-Jiro-Tsuji/100/i27 |archive-date=June 9, 2023 |access-date=2023-06-09 |website=cen.acs.org |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> was a Japanese chemist, notable for his discovery of organometallic reactions, including the [[Tsuji–Trost reaction]], the [[Tsuji–Wilkinson decarbonylation reaction]], and the [[Wacker process|Tsuji–Wacker reaction]].

== Early life and education ==
Tsuji was born in Japan in 1927.<ref name=":0" />

After attending [[Kyoto University]], Tsuji began his doctoral research at [[Columbia University]] under [[Gilbert Stork]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yamamoto |first=Y. |date=March 1999 |title=A profile of Professor Jiro Tsuji |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0022328X98011358 |journal=Journal of Organometallic Chemistry |language=en |volume=576 |issue=1–2 |pages=xi–xiii |doi=10.1016/S0022-328X(98)01135-8|url-access=subscription }}</ref> studying natural product synthesis, and making contributions to research on the dissolving metal reduction of enones.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Stork |first1=Gilbert |last2=Tsuji |first2=Jiro |date=June 1961 |title=LITHIUM-AMMONIA REDUCTION OF α,β-UNSATURATED KETONES. II. FORMATION AND ALKYLATION OF A β-CARBANION INTERMEDIATE |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja01473a053 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=83 |issue=12 |pages=2783–2784 |doi=10.1021/ja01473a053 |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Stork |first1=Gilbert |last2=Rosen |first2=P. |last3=Goldman |first3=N. |last4=Coombs |first4=R. V. |last5=Tsuji |first5=J. |date=January 1965 |title=Alkylation and Carbonation of Ketones by Trapping the Enolates from the Reduction of α,β-Unsaturated Ketones |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja01080a025 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=87 |issue=2 |pages=275–286 |doi=10.1021/ja01080a025 |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Independent career ==

His independent career began at Toyo Rayon (now [[Toray Industries]]) studying the stoichiometric, and later catalytic<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=Jiro. |last2=Kiji |first2=Jitsuo. |last3=Imamura |first3=Shinzo. |last4=Morikawa |first4=Masanobu. |date=October 1964 |title=Organic Syntheses by Means of Noble Metal Compounds. VIII. 1 Catalytic Carbonylation of Allylic Compounds with Palladium Chloride |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja01074a023 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=86 |issue=20 |pages=4350–4353 |doi=10.1021/ja01074a023 |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref> carbonylation of Pd<sup>II</sup>-alkene complexes with carbon monoxide.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=J. |last2=Morikawa |first2=M. |last3=Kiji |first3=J. |date=January 1963 |title=Reaction of olefin-palladium chloride complex with carbon monoxide. |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040403901907749 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=4 |issue=16 |pages=1061–1064 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)90774-9|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=Jiro |last2=Kiji |first2=Jitsuo |last3=Morikawa |first3=Masanobu |date=January 1963 |title=Organic syntheses by means of noble metal compounds III. Reaction of π -allylpalladium chloride complex with carbon monoxide |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040403901909207 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=4 |issue=26 |pages=1811–1813 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)90920-7|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His preliminary results showed that acyl halides and aldehydes could be decarbonylated by Pd<sup>0</sup> at high temperatures (200&nbsp;°C) yielding alkenes;<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=Jiro |last2=Ohno |first2=Kiyotaka |last3=Kajimoto |first3=Tsunesuke |date=January 1965 |title=Organic syntheses by means of noble metal compounds XX. Decarbonylation of acyl chloride and aldehyde catalyzed by palladium and its relationship with the rosenmund reduction. |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040403901890651 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=6 |issue=50 |pages=4565–4568 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)89065-1|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  further investigation revealed that stoichiometric quantities of [[Wilkinson's catalyst]] was able to affect the same reaction at lower temperatures,<ref name="Tsuji 3969–3971">{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=Jiro |last2=Ohno |first2=Kiyotaka |date=1965-01-01 |title=Organic syntheses by means of noble metal compounds XXI. Decarbonylation of aldehydes using rhodium complex |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0040403901891279 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=6 |issue=44 |pages=3969–3971 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)89127-9 |issn=0040-4039|url-access=subscription }}</ref> now known as the [[Tsuji–Wilkinson decarbonylation reaction]].
[[File:Tsuji-wilkinson first report.png|center|thumb|474x474px|Tsuji's first report of rhodium-mediated decarbonylation.<ref name="Tsuji 3969–3971"/>]]
His pioneering work resulting in the development of the [[Tsuji–Trost reaction]] was the discovery that allyl-Pd<sup>II</sup> complexes react with malonates, acetoacetates, and enamines yielding alpha-allylated carbonyl compounds,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=Jiro |last2=Takahashi |first2=Hidetaka |last3=Morikawa |first3=Masanobu |date=1965 |title=Organic syntheses by means of noble metal compounds XVII. Reaction of π-allylpalladium chloride with nucleophiles |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040403900716741 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=6 |issue=49 |pages=4387–4388 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(00)71674-1|url-access=subscription }}</ref> which was later generalized and rendered asymmetric by [[Barry Trost]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Trost |first1=Barry M. |last2=Fullerton |first2=Terry J. |date=January 1973 |title=New synthetic reactions. Allylic alkylation |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja00782a080 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=95 |issue=1 |pages=292–294 |doi=10.1021/ja00782a080 |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Tsuji additionally noted the utility of these alpha-allylated ketones and esters in preparing 1,4-dicarbonyl compounds using the [[Wacker oxidation]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=Jiro |last2=Shimizu |first2=Isao |last3=Yamamoto |first3=Keiji |date=August 1976 |title=Convenient general synthetic method for 1,4- and 1,5-diketones by palladium catalyzed oxidation of α-allyl and α-3-butenyl ketones |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040403901855040 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=17 |issue=34 |pages=2975–2976 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)85504-0|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
[[File:Tsuji-trost first report.png|center|thumb|473x473px|Tsuji's first report of palladium-mediated allylation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tsuji |first1=Jiro |last2=Takahashi |first2=Hidetaka |last3=Morikawa |first3=Masanobu |date=1965-01-01 |title=Organic syntheses by means of noble metal compounds XVII. Reaction of π-allylpalladium chloride with nucleophiles |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0040403900716741 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=6 |issue=49 |pages=4387–4388 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(00)71674-1 |issn=0040-4039|url-access=subscription }}</ref>]]
Later research hinged on the discovery that allyl acetoacetates decarboxylate and regioselectively ''alpha''-allylate in the presence of catalytic Pd(OAc)<sub>2</sub> and PPh<sub>3</sub> ''via'' the intermediacy of an allylpalladium enolate<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shimizu |first1=Isao |last2=Yamada |first2=Toshiro |last3=Tsuji |first3=Jiro |date=January 1980 |title=Palladium-catalyzed rearrangement of allylic esters of acetoacetic acid to give γ,δ-unsaturated methyl ketones |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0040403900774442 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |language=en |volume=21 |issue=33 |pages=3199–3202 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(00)77444-2|url-access=subscription }}</ref> - a catalytic [[Carroll rearrangement]]. Following work revealed that replacement of PPh<sub>3</sub> in the reaction mixture with the bidentate ligand [[1,2-Bis(diphenylphosphino)ethane|dppe]] could favor ''beta''-hydride elimination of the palladium enolate, yielding enones.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shimizu |first1=Isao |last2=Tsuji |first2=Jiro |date=October 1982 |title=Palladium-catalyzed decarboxylation-dehydrogenation of allyl .beta.-oxo carboxylates and allyl enol carbonates as a novel synthetic method for .alpha.-substituted .alpha.,.beta.-unsaturated ketones |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja00385a075 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=104 |issue=21 |pages=5844–5846 |doi=10.1021/ja00385a075 |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This transformation was applied by Tsuji to the racemic synthesis of [[methyl jasmonate]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kataoka |first1=Hideaki |last2=Yamada |first2=Toshiro |last3=Goto |first3=Kuniaki |last4=Tsuji |first4=Jiro |date=1987-01-01 |title=An efficiemt synthetic method of methyl (±)-jasmonate |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0040402001834499 |journal=Tetrahedron |language=en |volume=43 |issue=18 |pages=4107–4112 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4020(01)83449-9 |issn=0040-4020|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Tsuji also found that the palladium enolate could be engaged in intramolecular aldol reactions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nokami |first1=Junzo |last2=Mandai |first2=Tadakatsu |last3=Watanabe |first3=Hisayuki |last4=Ohyama |first4=Hiroshi |last5=Tsuji |first5=Jiro |date=May 1989 |title=The palladium-catalyzed directed aldol reaction of aldehydes with ketone enolates generated by the decarboxylation of allyl .beta.-keto carboxylates under neutral conditions |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja00193a069 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=111 |issue=11 |pages=4126–4127 |doi=10.1021/ja00193a069 |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Awards ==
* 1980 - Chemical Society of Japan Award, for "research on new organic synthesis processes using transition metal compounds"
* 1994 - [[Medals of Honor (Japan)|Purple ribbon medal of honor]]
* 2004 - Japan Academy Prize, for "research on new organic synthesis reactions using palladium catalysts"<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2004 |title=Prof. Jiro Tsuji and Prof. Akira Suzuki received the Japan Academy Prize |url=http://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/yukigoseikyokaishi1943/62/5/62_5_410/_article/-char/ja/ |journal=Journal of Synthetic Organic Chemistry, Japan |volume=62 |issue=5 |pages=410 |doi=10.5059/yukigoseikyokaishi.62.410 |issn=0037-9980 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609204947/https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/yukigoseikyokaishi1943/62/5/62_5_410/_article/-char/ja/ |archive-date=June 9, 2023 |doi-access=free |access-date=June 9, 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>
* 2014 - [[Tetrahedron Prize]]
* 2016 - [[Asian Scientist 100]], ''[[Asian Scientist]]''
